result:
Round 129 (V-0.2a) is implemented: the edit-command status messages and their Undo history labels are now English, coming from a new `studioEditStrings` object in `strings.ts`. One required check did not pass: mutation **m4 survived**, because no UI test checks the delete-clip status message. The rest of §4 is green. The report is in `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-129.md`.

**What changed (only the 12 granted paths: 11 modified, doc 105 new)**
- **`strings.ts`:** new `studioEditStrings` with E1–E42 (28 plain strings, 23 formatters). X1 now reads "The time selection is invalid — no file was created." The module still imports nothing.
- **`ArrangementContext.tsx`:** the 6 old Georgian constants are deleted and their uses point at the module; `LOOP_STEP_BLOCKED_MESSAGE` stays. The 8 commands use module strings. No condition, call order or dependency array changed; the conditional choices stay in the Context.
- **`strings.test.ts`:** ST6–ST9 added (5 → 9 tests), X1 updated in ST1.
- **The 8 dependent tests:** Georgian literals replaced by module references with the same matcher; track names kept. The `it` count is unchanged in every file except strings.

**Deviations for B to rule on**
- Where a test checked part of a Georgian message rather than the whole text, I used English fragments with the same matcher: `'the clipboard did not change'`, `'the gap was closed'`, `'marker'`. No module value matches those fragments. Kept in Georgian, the `not.toContain` checks would always pass and the `toContain` checks would always fail.
- I deleted the 6 constants rather than pointing them at the module; §2(b) allows either.

**Checks run**
- `npm run typecheck` passes, and `npm run lint` exits 0 (218 warnings, none in the changed files). Read-only Biome on the 11 changed code files is clean.
- `npx vitest run` on the 19-file list in `a-round-129/vitest-list.txt`: 19 files, 386 tests, all green on the final tree.
- **Mutations:**
  - m1 (Georgian `deleteClipDone`) turned ST6, ST8 and ST4 red.
  - m2 (Georgian history label in Split) turned ST9 red.
  - m3 (plural formatter ignoring the count) turned ST7 red.
  - m4 survived. The gap already existed before this round: the Georgian text had no test hits either. Adding an assertion is outside my grant, so it is open for B: one assertion in `delete-selection-ui` would close it. Two extra mutations on messages the UI tests do check both turned red, so those messages are wired through the module correctly.
- **code-reviewer:** approve, 9/10, no Critical/High/Medium.
  - L1 fixed: the "no SFX track" check now uses `onTrack('SFX')`, the exact equivalent of the old Georgian.
  - L2 (English fragments stop checking if the wording changes later) and L3 (the one-letter `e` alias in `strings.test.ts`) are reported to B, not changed.
  - The review wrongly says m4 was caught; it survived.
- **Architecture note for B/root:** keep both files as they are. Decide "conditional text inside formatters vs in the Context" at the frontend-architect checkpoint already planned after V-0.2c.

**State**
- Frozen list OK at start and end; protected files unchanged versus `77f2763`. The 12 end hashes are in `a-round-129/end-sha256.txt`.
- All lasting edits were made with Edit/Write. The shell writes were the temporary mutation edits (restored, sha256 OK) and one empty temp file I created by mistake and removed at once; all are listed in the report.
- Not run: the full suite, verify, build and any browser check; those belong to the gate and to C.
- Until track names are translated (V-0.4/V-0.5), a status can still read "on the მუსიკა track", as the task decided.

**Next for C:** the §5 rows on `http://127.0.0.1:5173/studio-lab`. Pay particular attention to:
- the single-clip delete message in the browser, since no unit test covers it;
- Cut Time with a marker inside;
- Paste with and without the "on the … track" suffix;
- the Undo button width with "Delete time selection (all tracks)".
